# gr-fosphor

**GPU-drawn real-time spectrum and waterfall display blocks for GNU Radio**

- **Version recorded:** 3.9~git20240323.74d54fc
- **Categories:** `sdr-toolkits`
- **Upstream:** <https://gitea.osmocom.org/sdr/gr-fosphor>

## What it does

Adds fosphor sink blocks to GNU Radio Companion: a spectrum display and a waterfall computed and drawn on the graphics card through OpenCL and OpenGL, fast enough to show tens of MHz of bandwidth as a smooth live picture with a persistence ("phosphor") trace. There is a Qt sink for use inside a Qt GUI flow graph and a GLFW sink that opens its own window, plus an overlap block for the FFT input.

## Why you would want it

A CPU-drawn FFT display in GNU Radio stutters or drops samples at the wide sample rates a HackRF, bladeRF or USRP can deliver. fosphor moves the FFT and the drawing to the GPU, so a wide band can be watched live, and its persistence view shows short bursts that a normal waterfall averages away. It is the display most GNU Radio demonstrations use. It is an alternative to GNU Radio's own QT GUI Frequency and Waterfall sinks, which need no GPU.

## Before it will work

GNU Radio (it arrives as a dependency) and a working OpenCL platform with OpenGL on the same device, which apt does NOT install for you. Install the OpenCL driver for your graphics hardware and check it with `clinfo` before opening a flow graph. The 2026-09-30 sweep found `mesa-opencl-icd`, `pocl-opencl-icd` and `clinfo` offered on Debian 13, Parrot and Ubuntu 24.04; Intel's own `intel-opencl-icd` was offered on Ubuntu 24.04 and not in the main component of Debian 13 or Parrot. Which one works with fosphor on which GPU is unmeasured here.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profile:** [`sdr`](../profiles/sdr.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install gr-fosphor --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `gr-fosphor`
  - The .deb Depends on `gnuradio-dev` (read from Debian 13's control file, 2026-09-30), so installing it pulls GNU Radio's development headers as well as GNU Radio. Its library Depends on `ocl-icd-libopencl1 | libopencl1`, which is the OpenCL loader only: no OpenCL driver for any GPU comes with it.

## Known problems

Unmeasured on any machine here, including the field laptop's Intel Iris Xe: no fosphor block has been run. Its dependencies name only the OpenCL loader, so nothing at install time notices a machine with no OpenCL driver; that shows up when a flow graph with a fosphor sink starts. The install is larger than the package suggests, because it pulls `gnuradio-dev`. Upstream has had no commit since 2024-03-23.
